steps.prompt: You have spent $6$ minutes on question $12$ and you're still stuck. What do you do next, and why?

cards.title: What a guess is worth
cards.body: A guess among $n$ choices is right with chance $\frac{1}{n}$, so on average it is worth $\frac{6}{n}$ points. A blank is worth $1.5$. Guess when $\frac{6}{n} > 1.5$, which means $n < 4$: rule out at least $2$ choices first. With $1$ ruled out, guessing and a blank are worth the same.

cards.title: The 2-minute rule
cards.body: If you have spent about $2$ minutes on a question and still have no plan, mark it and move on. A hard question is worth the same $6$ points as an easy one, and there are easier points further along. Come back to the marked questions at the end with fresh eyes.

cards.title: Worked example: guess or blank?
cards.problem: On $4$ questions you can rule out $2$ choices each. On $3$ more you can't rule out any. If you guess on the $4$ and leave the $3$ blank, how many points do you expect from these $7$ questions?

steps.text: A guess among $3$ choices is worth $\frac{6}{3} = 2$ points on average, so the $4$ guesses are worth $4 \times 2 = 8$.
In total you expect $8 + 4.5 = 12.5$ points. Guessing on all $7$ would give $8 + 3 \times 1.2 = 11.6$: less, because blind guesses are worth only $1.2$ each.

cards.title: Worked example: your own guessing record
cards.problem: When you mark an answer "Guessing", you have been right $20\%$ of the time. Should you answer those questions or leave them blank?

steps.text: Each of those answers earns $6$ points $20\%$ of the time.

try.prompt: On average, how many points is one of those answers worth?

steps.text: $0.2 \times 6 = 1.2$ points: less than a blank's $1.5$. Leave those blank.

try.prompt: What fraction of the time would you need to be right for answering to equal a blank?

steps.text: Break even is $\frac{1.5}{6} = \frac{1}{4}$, or $25\%$. Your progress page shows how often each of your confidence levels is right.

cards.title: The common trap: "I've already spent so long on it"
cards.body: The minutes you have spent are gone whether you finish the question or not. Ask only what the next minutes are worth: one stuck question, or two fresh ones further along.

prompts: Write your own rule for when you will guess, leave a blank, or skip and come back.
